Fit G2G Model with Time-Varying Covariates

Source: R/G2G_varying_functions.R
G2G_varying_MLE.Rd

Fits a Grassia(II)-Geometric (G2G) survival model with time-varying covariates using maximum likelihood estimation. Covariates are centered and scaled internally to keep the likelihood numerically stable, and the results are converted back to the original covariate scale.

Usage

G2G_varying_MLE(fo, data, subject, level = 0.95)

Arguments

fo

Formula object specifying the model in the format Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2 + ... where time is the observation time, status is the event indicator, and x1, x2, etc. are time-varying covariates. Note: The formula should use variable names, not column indices. Only plain variable names are allowed on the right-hand side: transformations such as log(x), I(x^2) or factor(x) and interactions such as x1 * x2 are rejected with an error (they would otherwise be silently ignored). Create transformed variables as new columns in data first.

data

Data frame containing all variables specified in the formula. Data should be in long format with one row per time point per subject (person-period format). Rows are sorted by subject and time internally. Within each subject, the time variable must run 1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps or duplicates. A subject counts as having had an event if the status variable is 1 on any of their rows, and the event is placed in the subject's last period.

subject

Character string specifying the name of the subject ID column in the data frame. This column identifies which observations belong to the same subject over time.

level

Confidence level for the Wald confidence intervals, a single number strictly between 0 and 1. Default is 0.95.

Value

A list of class "G2Gcov" containing the optimization results from optim with additional elements. All estimates, standard errors and confidence bounds are reported on the original covariate scale (only hessian is on the internal parameterization):

par

Parameter estimates. First two are r and alpha (shape and rate parameters), remaining are covariate coefficients in original units.

par_stderr

Standard errors of parameter estimates (named like par). For r and alpha these come from the delta method, e.g. SE(r) is approximately r * SE(log r). If the Hessian is not positive definite (or cannot be inverted) a warning is issued and these are NA.

par_upper

Upper bounds of the Wald confidence intervals at the requested level. For r and alpha the interval is formed on the log scale and exponentiated.

par_lower

Lower bounds of the Wald confidence intervals at the requested level

level

The confidence level used for par_lower and par_upper

value

Negative log-likelihood at the optimum

convergence

Convergence code (0 indicates successful convergence; a warning is issued for any other code)

hessian

Hessian matrix at the optimum, on the internal parameterization (log r, log alpha, standardized coefficients), with row and column names

center

Covariate means used internally for centering

scale

Covariate standard deviations used internally for scaling

terms

The terms object for the covariates, used to code new data in G2G_varying_survival

xlevels

Factor levels of the covariates at fitting time, also used to code new data

Examples

# \donttest{
  data(kb_data)
  kb_data$status <- 1L - kb_data$censor
  fit <- G2G_varying_MLE(
    "Surv(week, status) ~ coupon + anyp",
    data    = kb_data,
    subject = "id"
  )
#> Warning: The Hessian at the solution is not positive definite (or could not be inverted), so standard errors and confidence intervals are NA.
  print(fit)
#> G2G Model Fit
#> ---------------------------------------------------- 
#> Convergence:       Converged (code 0)
#> Log-likelihood:    -5612.1808
#> AIC:               11232.3616
#> Parameters:        4
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>                Estimate Std.Error Lower.95 Upper.95
#> r (shape)     2996.6875        NA       NA       NA
#> alpha (rate) 40722.0679        NA       NA       NA
#> coupon         -78.2544        NA       NA       NA
#> anyp             0.0020        NA       NA       NA
#> 
#> Note: some standard errors are NA (the Hessian at the optimum is singular or not positive definite).

  # 90% confidence intervals instead of the default 95%
  fit90 <- G2G_varying_MLE(
    "Surv(week, status) ~ coupon + anyp",
    data    = kb_data,
    subject = "id",
    level   = 0.90
  )
#> Warning: The Hessian at the solution is not positive definite (or could not be inverted), so standard errors and confidence intervals are NA.
# }
